question: Does the alfworld-flash study's gate-accepted skill improvement replicate on a fresh run measured with the revised standard (3 final-test repeats), and how large is same-skill noise on this panel at 3 repeats?

task_source.benchmark: ALFWorld (MIT); identical deterministic pack and frozen 6-seen + 6-unseen test games as alfworld-flash

settings.workspace: fresh (the original workspace cannot raise repeats: the frozen protocol is immutable by design)

search_outcomes.reason: proposal and training change no files

candidate.note: identical initial skills - nothing was accepted in this run

final_panel_test_12_games_x3_repeats.per_split: all unseen layouts solved 6/6 in every condition and repeat; variation concentrates on seen layouts

replication_verdict: NOT REPLICATED. The original run's accepted +0.125 validation gain and +2-game frozen-panel margin sit inside the same-skill noise measured here: baseline and candidate carry identical skills yet differ by 0.083 mean (one game) across 3-repeat draws, and per-repeat scores of every condition swing within [0.75, 1.0]. The original study's one-game candidate-vs-no-skills margin was already flagged as within noise; the two-game candidate-vs-initial-skill margin must now be read the same way. The honest platform-level claim survives: the full gated lifecycle runs on real engine-scored tasks and the gate blocks harmful edits; single-run acceptances at this panel size are noise-dominated, which is the measured motivation for the selector-study protocol and noise-band gate.
audit: zero expected-answer leakage, zero silent bypass; verify lineage ok; reports/noise-band.json generated by the standard report command
limits: One replication run, one seed, flash tier. A non-replication at n=2 does not prove the original effect was pure noise (both runs' search outcomes are draws from the same noisy process); it does show that single-run gate acceptances on this panel cannot be treated as reproducible evidence. Multi-seed orchestration remains the open prerequisite named in the selector-study protocol.
